evals.prompt: Can you review my PR? It renames `getUserData` to `fetchUserProfile` across 14 files and fixes a typo in the README. Tests pass locally.
evals.expected_output: Proportionate review: checks the rename is complete and consistent with codebase naming conventions (fetch vs get), looks for missed dynamic references and string usages, notes that the author's local test run is not the reviewer's observation. Produces an Approve or Approve with comments verdict with few findings; no invented issues or nit avalanche.
expectations: Checks for missed references (dynamic/string usages, docs, mocks) of the old name
Considers whether the new name matches existing naming conventions in the codebase
Does not claim tests pass as Observed unless the reviewer ran them
Does not invent unrelated blockers; verdict is proportionate to a low-risk change

evals.prompt: Before you tell me you're done with the payment webhook handler you just wrote, do a self-review.
evals.expected_output: Runs the self-review with the same checklist: webhook signature verification over the raw body, timestamp tolerance, idempotency by event ID, timeouts on outbound calls, error handling, secrets not logged, tests that would fail when broken. Fixes Blockers and Majors before reporting, lists checks run and what was not checked.
expectations: Checks webhook signature verification and replay protection
Reports the checks actually run (tests, type check, lint) separately from what was not checked
Fixes or explicitly lists any Blocker/Major findings before declaring done
